cues.en: Mathematics began as a way to quantify our world,
cues.zh: 数学最初是为了量化我们的世界，

cues.en: to measure land, predict the motions of planets, and keep track of commerce.
cues.zh: 测量土地、预测行星运动，以及记录商业活动。

cues.en: Then came a problem considered impossible.
cues.zh: 后来出现了一个被认为不可能解决的问题。

cues.en: The secret to solving it was to separate math from the real world, to split algebra from geometry,
cues.zh: 解决它的秘诀在于将数学与现实世界分离，将代数与几何分开，

cues.en: and to invent new numbers so fanciful they are called imaginary.
cues.zh: 并发明出如此奇幻的新数字，以至于它们被称为虚数。

cues.en: Ironically,
cues.zh: 讽刺的是，

cues.en: four hundred years later, these very numbers turn up in the heart of our best physical theory of the universe.
cues.zh: 四百年后，正是这些数字出现在我们最优秀的宇宙物理理论的核心。

cues.en: Only by abandoning mass connection to reality could we discover reality's true nature.
cues.zh: 只有放弃与现实的紧密联系，我们才能发现现实的真正本质。

cues.en: Luca Pacioli,
cues.zh: Luca Pacioli，

cues.en: who is Leonardo da Vinci's math teacher, publishes Summa de Arithmetica,
cues.zh: 也就是Leonardo da Vinci的数学老师，出版了《算术大全》，

cues.en: a comprehensive summary of all mathematics known in Renaissance Italy at the time.
cues.zh: 这是当时文艺复兴时期意大利已知全部数学的综合总结。

cues.en: In it, there is a section on the cubic, any equation which today we would write as a x cubed plus b x squared plus c x plus d equals zero.
cues.zh: 书中有一节讲三次方程，也就是今天我们会写成 a x 立方加 b x 平方加 c x 加 d 等于零的任何方程。

cues.en: People have been trying to find a general solution to the cubic for at least four thousand years.
cues.zh: 人们试图找到三次方程的一般解法，至少已有四千年。

cues.en: But each ancient civilization that encountered it, the Babylonians,
cues.zh: 但每一个遇到它的古代文明，巴比伦人、

cues.en: Greeks, Chinese, Indians, Egyptians, and Persians,
cues.zh: 希腊人、中国人、印度人、埃及人和波斯人，

cues.en: they all came up empty handed.
cues.zh: 全都一无所获。

cues.en: Pacioli's conclusion is that a solution to the cubic equation is impossible.
cues.zh: Pacioli的结论是，三次方程的解法是不可能的。

cues.en: Now this should be at least a little surprising since without the x cubed term, the equation is simply a quadratic.
cues.zh: 这至少应该有点令人意外，因为如果没有 x 立方项，这个方程就只是二次方程。

cues.en: And many ancient civilizations had solved quadratics thousands of years earlier.
cues.zh: 而许多古代文明早在数千年前就已经解出了二次方程。

cues.en: Today, anyone who's passed eighth grade knows the general solution. It's minus b plus minus root b squared minus four a c all over two a.
cues.zh: 今天，任何一个上过八年级的人都知道这个通解。就是负b加减根号下b平方减4ac，再除以2a。

cues.en: But most people just plug and chug into this formula completely oblivious
cues.zh: 但大多数人只是直接套公式，完全不知道

cues.en: to the geometry that ancient mathematicians used
cues.zh: 古代数学家用来推导它的几何方法。

cues.en: to derive it. You know, back in those days, mathematics wasn't written down in equations.
cues.zh: 你知道，在那个年代，数学并不是用方程写下来的。

cues.en: It was written with words and pictures.
cues.zh: 而是用文字和图形写成的。

cues.en: Take for example the equation x squared plus 26 x equals 27.
cues.zh: 举个例子，方程x平方加26x等于27。

cues.en: Ancient mathematicians would think of the x squared term like a literal square with sides of length x.
cues.zh: 古代数学家会把x平方这一项想成一个边长为x的正方形。

cues.en: And then 26 x, well, would be a rectangle
cues.zh: 然后26x呢，就是一个长方形

cues.en: with one side of length 26
cues.zh: 一边长26

cues.en: and the other side of length x.
cues.zh: 另一边长x。

cues.en: And these two areas together
cues.zh: 这两个面积加起来

cues.en: add to 27.
cues.zh: 等于27。

cues.en: So how do we figure out what x is?
cues.zh: 那我们怎么求出x是多少呢？

cues.en: Well, we can take this 26 x rectangle
cues.zh: 我们可以把这个26x的长方形

cues.en: and
cues.zh: 然后

cues.en: cut it in half.
cues.zh: 切成两半。

cues.en: So now I have two thirteen x rectangles
cues.zh: 现在我就有了两个13x的长方形

cues.en: and I can position them so the new shape I create is almost a square. It's just missing this section down here.
cues.zh: 我可以把它们摆好，让新形状差不多是个正方形。只差下面这一块。

cues.en: But I know the dimensions of this section, it's just 13 by 13.
cues.zh: 但我知道这一块的尺寸，就是13乘13。

cues.en: So I can complete the square
cues.zh: 所以我可以配成完全平方

cues.en: by adding in a 13 by 13
cues.zh: 通过补上一个13乘13的

cues.en: square.
cues.zh: 正方形。

cues.en: Now since I've added 13 squared or a 169
cues.zh: 既然我加了13的平方，也就是169

cues.en: to the left hand side of the equation, I also have to add a 169 to the right hand side of the equation
cues.zh: 到方程左边，我也得加169到方程右边

cues.en: to maintain the equality.
cues.zh: 来保持等式成立。

cues.en: So now I have this larger square with sides of length x plus 13
cues.zh: 现在我就有了这个更大的正方形，边长是x加13

cues.en: and it is equal to a 196.
cues.zh: 它等于196。

cues.en: Now the square root of a 196 is 14.
cues.zh: 196的平方根是14。

cues.en: So I know that the sides of this square have length 14,
cues.zh: 我知道这个正方形的边长是14，

cues.en: which means x is equal to one.
cues.zh: 这意味着x等于1。

cues.en: Now this is a great visual way to solve a quadratic equation,
cues.zh: 这是解二次方程的一种很好的可视化方法，

cues.en: but it isn't complete.
cues.zh: 但它并不完整。

cues.en: I mean, you look at our original equation, x equals one is a solution,
cues.zh: 我的意思是，看看我们原来的方程，x等于1是一个解，

cues.en: but so is negative 27.
cues.zh: 但-27也是。

cues.en: For thousands of years, mathematicians were oblivious to the negative solutions to their equations because they were dealing with things in the real world, lengths and areas and volumes. I mean, what would it mean to have a square with sides of length negative 27?
cues.zh: 几千年来，数学家们一直忽视方程中的负数解，因为他们处理的是现实世界中的东西——长度、面积和体积。我的意思是，一个边长为-27的正方形意味着什么呢？

cues.en: That just doesn't make any sense.
cues.zh: 这根本说不通。

cues.en: So for those mathematicians,
cues.zh: 所以对那些数学家来说，

cues.en: negative numbers didn't exist.
cues.zh: 负数并不存在。

cues.en: You could subtract, that is find the difference between two positive quantities, but you couldn't have a negative answer or negative coefficients.
cues.zh: 你可以做减法，也就是求两个正数之间的差，但你不能有负的结果或负的系数。

cues.en: Mathematicians were so averse to negative numbers that there was no single quadratic equation.
cues.zh: 数学家们对负数如此反感，以至于当时并不存在单一的二次方程。

cues.en: Instead, there were six different versions arranged so that the coefficients were always positive.
cues.zh: 取而代之的是六种不同的版本，排列方式确保系数始终为正。

cues.en: The same approach was taken with the cubic. In the eleventh century, Persian mathematician Omar Khayyam identified 19 different cubic equations.
cues.zh: 三次方程也采用了同样的方法。十一世纪，波斯数学家Omar Khayyam识别出了19种不同的三次方程。

cues.en: Again, keeping all coefficients positive.
cues.zh: 同样，保持所有系数为正。

cues.en: He found numerical solutions to some of them by considering the intersections of shapes like hyperbolas and circles.
cues.zh: 他通过考虑双曲线和圆等形状的交点，找到了其中一些方程的数值解。

cues.en: But he fell short of his ultimate goal, a general solution to the cubic.
cues.zh: 但他未能实现自己的终极目标——三次方程的通解。

cues.en: He wrote, maybe one of those who will come after us will succeed in finding it.
cues.zh: 他写道，也许我们之后的人里，会有人成功找到它。

cues.en: Four hundred years later and 4,000 kilometers away, the solution begins to take shape.
cues.zh: 四百年后，在四千公里之外，解法开始成形。

cues.en: Scipione Delferro is a mathematics professor at the University of Bologna.
cues.zh: Scipione Delferro 是博洛尼亚大学的数学教授。

cues.en: Sometime around 1510,
cues.zh: 大约在 1510 年的某天，

cues.en: he finds a method to reliably solve depressed cubics.
cues.zh: 他找到了一种可靠求解缺项三次方程的方法。

cues.en: These are a subset of cubic equations with no x squared term.
cues.zh: 这是一类没有 x 平方项的三次方程。

cues.en: So what does he do after solving a problem that has stumped mathematicians for millennia?
cues.zh: 那么，在解决了一个困扰数学家千年的问题之后，他做了什么？

cues.en: One considered impossible by Leonardo da Vinci's math teacher?
cues.zh: 一个被 Leonardo da Vinci 的数学老师认为不可能解决的问题？

cues.en: He tells
cues.zh: 他告诉

cues.en: no one.
cues.zh: 没有人。

cues.en: See, being a mathematician in the fifteen hundreds is hard. Your job is constantly under threat from other mathematicians who can show up at any time and challenge you for your position. You can think of it like a math duel.
cues.zh: 你看，在十六世纪当数学家很难。你的职位时刻受到其他数学家的威胁，他们随时可能出现，向你挑战职位。你可以把它想象成一场数学决斗。

cues.en: Each participant submits a set of questions to the other and the person who solves the most questions correctly gets the job,
cues.zh: 每位参与者向对方提交一组问题，答对最多的人得到职位，

cues.en: while the loser suffers public humiliation.
cues.zh: 而输家则遭受公开羞辱。

cues.en: As far as Del Ferro knows, no one else in the world can solve the depressed cubic. So by keeping his solution secret,
cues.zh: 据 Del Ferro 所知，世界上没有其他人能解缺项三次方程。所以通过保密他的解法，

cues.en: he guarantees
cues.zh: 他保证了

cues.en: his own job security.
cues.zh: 自己的职位安全。

cues.en: For nearly two decades, Del Ferro keeps his secret. Only on his deathbed in 1526
cues.zh: 近二十年里，Del Ferro 一直保守着秘密。直到 1526 年临终之际，

cues.en: does he let it slip to his student Antonio Fior.
cues.zh: 他才把这个秘密透露给学生 Antonio Fior。

cues.en: Fior is not as talented a mathematician as his mentor, but he is young and ambitious.
cues.zh: Fior 的数学才能不如他的导师，但他年轻且雄心勃勃。

cues.en: And after Delferro's death, he boasts about his own mathematical prowess and specifically
cues.zh: 在 Delferro 死后，他吹嘘自己的数学造诣，特别是

cues.en: his ability to solve the depressed cubic.
cues.zh: 他解缺项三次方程的能力。

cues.en: Fior challenges mathematician Niccolo Fontana Tartaglia,
cues.zh: 菲奥尔向数学家尼科洛·丰塔纳·塔尔塔利亚发起挑战，

cues.en: who has recently moved to Fior's hometown of Venice.
cues.zh: 后者最近刚搬到菲奥尔的家乡威尼斯。

cues.en: Niccolo Fontana is no stranger to adversity.
cues.zh: 尼科洛·丰塔纳对逆境并不陌生。

cues.en: As a kid, his face was cut open by a French soldier leaving him with a stutter. That's why he's known as Tartaglia,
cues.zh: 小时候，他的脸被一名法国士兵砍开，留下了口吃的毛病。这就是他被称为塔尔塔利亚的原因，

cues.en: which means stutterer in Italian.
cues.zh: 在意大利语中意为口吃者。

cues.en: Growing up in poverty, Tartaglia is largely self taught. He claws his way up through Italian society to become a respected mathematician.
cues.zh: 塔尔塔利亚在贫困中长大，基本靠自学成才。他一路奋斗跻身意大利社会，成为受人尊敬的数学家。

cues.en: Now,
cues.zh: 如今，

cues.en: all of that is at stake.
cues.zh: 这一切都岌岌可危。

cues.en: As is the custom in the challenge, Tartaglia gives a varied assortment of 30 problems to Fior.
cues.zh: 按照挑战的惯例，塔尔塔利亚给菲奥尔出了30道各不相同的题目。

cues.en: Fior gives 30 problems to Tartaglia,
cues.zh: 菲奥尔给塔尔塔利亚出了30道题，

cues.en: all of which are depressed cubics.
cues.zh: 全都是缺项三次方程。

cues.en: Each mathematician has forty days to solve the 30 problems they've been given.
cues.zh: 每位数学家都有四十天时间来解决收到的30道题。

cues.en: Fior can't solve a single problem.
cues.zh: 菲奥尔一道题都解不出来。

cues.en: Tartaglia
cues.zh: 塔尔塔利亚

cues.en: solves all 30 of Fior's depressed cubics in just two hours.
cues.zh: 仅用两个小时就解出了菲奥尔全部30道缺项三次方程。

cues.en: It seems Fior's boastfulness was his undoing.
cues.zh: 看来菲奥尔的吹嘘害了他自己。

cues.en: Before the challenge came, Tartaglia learns of Fior's claim to have solved the depressed cubic, but he's skeptical.
cues.zh: 挑战到来之前，塔尔塔利亚听说菲奥尔声称自己解出了缺项三次方程，但他对此表示怀疑。

cues.en: I did not deem him capable of finding such a rule on his own, Tartaglia writes. But word was that a great mathematician had revealed the secret to Fior, which seems more plausible.
cues.zh: “我不认为他能独自找到这样的法则，”塔尔塔利亚写道。“但传言说一位伟大的数学家向菲奥尔透露了这个秘密，这似乎更可信。”

cues.en: So with the knowledge that a solution to the cubic is possible and with his livelihood on the line, Tartaglia sets about solving the depressed cubic himself.
cues.zh: 于是，在得知三次方程确实有解、且自己的生计命悬一线的情况下，塔尔塔利亚开始亲自攻克缺项三次方程。

cues.en: To do it, he extends the idea of completing the square into three dimensions.
cues.zh: 他为此把配方法的思想扩展到了三维。

cues.en: Take the equation x cubed plus nine x equals 26.
cues.zh: 来看方程 x³ + 9x = 26。

cues.en: You can think of x cubed as the volume of a cube with sides of length x. And if you add a volume of nine x, you get 26.
cues.zh: 你可以把 x³ 想成边长是 x 的立方体的体积。再加上 9x 的体积，就得到 26。

cues.en: So just like with completing the square, we need to add onto the cube to increase its volume by nine x.
cues.zh: 所以就像配方法那样，我们要在这个立方体上补一块，让体积增加 9x。

cues.en: Imagine extending three sides of this cube out a distance y,
cues.zh: 想象把这个立方体的三条边各向外延伸 y 的距离，

cues.en: creating a new larger cube with sides of length, call it z.
cues.zh: 得到一个新的更大的立方体，边长记为 z。

cues.en: Z is just x plus y.
cues.zh: z 就是 x + y。

cues.en: The original cube has been padded out, and we can break up the additional volume into seven shapes.
cues.zh: 原来的立方体被填充扩展了，我们可以把增加出来的体积拆成七块形状。

cues.en: There are three rectangular prisms with dimensions of x by x by y
cues.zh: 其中三个是长方体，尺寸为 x × x × y，

cues.en: and another three narrower prisms with dimensions of x by y by y.
cues.zh: 另外三个是更窄的长方体，尺寸为 x × y × y。

cues.en: Plus, there's a cube with a volume y cubed.
cues.zh: 再加上一个体积为 y³ 的小立方体。

cues.en: Tertaglia rearranges the six rectangular prisms into one block.
cues.zh: Tartaglia 把这六个长方体重新拼成一个块。

cues.en: One side has length three y, the other has a length x plus y, which is z, and the height is x.
cues.zh: 它的一边长度是 3y，另一边长度是 x + y，也就是 z，高是 x。

cues.en: So the volume of this shape is its base three y z times its height x. And Tartaglia realizes this volume can perfectly represent the nine x term in the equation
cues.zh: 所以这个形状的体积是底面积 3yz 乘以高 x。Tartaglia 发现这个体积恰好能表示方程中的 9x 项，

cues.en: if its base is equal to nine. So he sets three y z equals nine.
cues.zh: 只要它的底面积等于 9。于是他令 3yz = 9。

cues.en: Putting the cube back together, you find we're missing the one small y cubed block. So we can complete the cube by adding y cubed to both sides of the equation.
cues.zh: 把大立方体重新拼回去，你会发现我们还缺那个小的 y³ 立方块。所以只要在方程两边都加上 y³，就能补全这个立方体。

cues.en: Now we have z cubed, the complete larger cube equals 26 plus y cubed. We have two equations and two unknowns.
cues.zh: 现在我们有 z³，也就是完整的更大立方体，等于 26 + y³。我们有了两个方程和两个未知数。

cues.en: Solving the first equation for z and substituting into the second, we get y to the six plus 26 y cubed equals 27.
cues.zh: 解第一个方程得到 z，再代入第二个方程，我们得到 y 的六次方加上 26 倍的 y 的三次方等于 27。

cues.en: At first glance, it seems like we're now worse off than when we started. The variable is now raised to the power of six instead of just three.
cues.zh: 乍一看，我们似乎比开始时更糟了。这个变量现在被提升到了六次方，而不是三次方。

cues.en: However,
cues.zh: 不过，

cues.en: if you think of y cubed as a new variable,
cues.zh: 如果你把 y 的三次方看作一个新的变量，

cues.en: the equation is actually a quadratic.
cues.zh: 这个方程实际上就是一个二次方程。

cues.en: The same quadratic that we solved by completing the square.
cues.zh: 正是我们之前通过配方法解出的那个二次方程。

cues.en: So we know y cubed equals one, which means y equals one. And z equals three over y, so z is three. And since x plus y equals z, x must be equal to two,
cues.zh: 于是我们知道 y 的三次方等于 1，这意味着 y 等于 1。而 z 等于 3 除以 y，所以 z 是 3。又因为 x 加 y 等于 z，所以 x 必定等于 2，

cues.en: which is indeed a solution to the original equation.
cues.zh: 这确实是原方程的一个解。

cues.en: And with that, Tartaglia becomes the second human on the planet to solve the depressed cubic.
cues.zh: 至此，Tartaglia 成为地球上第二个解出降次三次方程的人。

cues.en: To save himself the work of going through the geometry for each new cubic he encounters, Tartaglia summarizes his method in an algorithm,
cues.zh: 为了省去每遇到一个新三次方程都要重新走一遍几何推导的麻烦，Tartaglia 把他的方法总结成了一个算法，

cues.en: a set of instructions.
cues.zh: 一组指令。

cues.en: He writes this down not as a set of equations like we would today, modern algebraic notation wouldn't exist for another hundred years, but instead as a poem.
cues.zh: 他写下的不是像我们今天这样的一组方程——现代代数符号还要再过一百年才出现——而是一首诗。

cues.en: Tartaglia's victory makes him something of a celebrity.
cues.zh: Tartaglia 的胜利让他成了某种名人。

cues.en: Mathematicians are desperate to learn how he solved the cubic, especially Girolamo Cardano, a polymath based in Milan.
cues.zh: 数学家们急切地想了解他是如何解出三次方程的，尤其是 Girolamo Cardano，一位常驻米兰的博学家。

cues.en: As you can guess, Cartaglia will have none of it. He refuses to reveal even a single question from the competition.
cues.zh: 你可以猜到，Tartaglia 根本不买账。他连竞赛中的一道题都不肯透露。

cues.en: But Cardano is persistent.
cues.zh: 但 Cardano 很执着。

cues.en: He writes a series of letters that alternate between flattery and aggressive attacks.
cues.zh: 他写了一连串信，在奉承和猛烈攻击之间来回切换。

cues.en: Eventually,
cues.zh: 最终，

cues.en: with the promise of an introduction to his wealthy benefactor,
cues.zh: 以把他引荐给自己富有的赞助人为承诺，

cues.en: Cardano
cues.zh: Cardano

cues.en: manages to lure Tartaglia to Milan.
cues.zh: 成功把 Tartaglia 诱到了米兰。

cues.en: And there, on 03/25/1539,
cues.zh: 就在那里，1539年3月25日，

cues.en: Tartaglia reveals his method. But only after forcing Cardano to swear a solemn oath not to tell anyone the method, not to publish it, and to write it only in cipher,
cues.zh: Tartaglia 公开了他的方法。但在此之前，他强迫 Cardano 郑重发誓：不把方法告诉任何人，不发表，并且只用密码写下来，

cues.en: quote, so that after my death,
cues.zh: 原话是：这样在我死后，

cues.en: no one shall be able to understand it.
cues.zh: 没人能看懂它。

cues.en: Cardano is delighted and immediately starts playing around with Tartaglia's algorithm.
cues.zh: Cardano 很高兴，立刻开始摆弄 Tartaglia 的算法。

cues.en: But he has a loftier goal in mind, a solution to the full cubic equation including the x squared term.
cues.zh: 但他心里有个更高的目标：解出包含 x 平方项的完整三次方程。

cues.en: And amazingly,
cues.zh: 而令人惊讶的是，

cues.en: he discovers it. If you substitute for x,
cues.zh: 他发现了它。如果你把 x 替换为

cues.en: x minus b over three a, then all the x squared terms cancel out. This
cues.zh: x - b/(3a)，那么所有 x 平方项都会消掉。这

cues.en: is the way to turn any general cubic equation into a depressed cubic, which can then be solved by Tartaglia's formula.
cues.zh: 就是把任意一般三次方程化为缺项三次方程的方法，然后就能用 Tartaglia 的公式求解。

cues.en: Cardano is so excited to have solved the problem that stumped the best mathematicians for thousands of years, he wants to publish it.
cues.zh: Cardano 解决了困扰顶尖数学家数千年的问题，兴奋不已，想把它发表出来。

cues.en: Unlike his peers, Cardano has no need to keep the solution a secret. He makes his living not as a mathematician,
cues.zh: 与同行不同，Cardano 没必要把解法保密。他谋生靠的不是数学家身份，

cues.en: but as a physician and famous intellectual.
cues.zh: 而是医生和著名知识分子的身份。

cues.en: For him, the credit is more valuable than the secret.
cues.zh: 对他来说，功劳比保密更有价值。

cues.en: The only problem is the oath he swore to Tartaglia
cues.zh: 唯一的问题是，他向 Tartaglia 发过的誓

cues.en: who won't let him break it.
cues.zh: 而 Tartaglia 不会让他违背誓言。

cues.en: And you might think this would be the end of it, but in 1542,
cues.zh: 你可能以为事情到此为止了，但在1542年，

cues.en: Cardano travels to Bologna and there he visits a mathematician who just happens to be the son-in-law of one Del Ferro, the man who, on his deathbed, gave the solution to the depressed cubic to Antonio Fior.
cues.zh: 卡尔达诺前往博洛尼亚，在那里拜访了一位数学家，此人恰好是德尔费罗的女婿——德尔费罗临终前把缺项三次方程的解法传授给了安东尼奥·菲奥尔。

cues.en: Cardano finds this solution in Del Ferro's old notebook, which is shared with him during the visit.
cues.zh: 卡尔达诺在德尔费罗的旧笔记本里找到了这个解法，拜访期间对方把笔记本拿给他看了。

cues.en: This solution predates Tartaglia's
cues.zh: 这个解法比塔尔塔利亚的

cues.en: by decades.
cues.zh: 早了几十年。

cues.en: So now, as Cardano sees it, he can publish the full solution to the cubic without
cues.zh: 所以在卡尔达诺看来，他现在可以发表三次方程的完整解法，

cues.en: violating his oath to Tartaglia.
cues.zh: 而不算违背对塔尔塔利亚的誓言。

cues.en: Three years later, Cardano publishes Ars Magna, The Great Art, an updated compendium of mathematics.
cues.zh: 三年后，卡尔达诺出版了《大衍术》（Ars Magna），一部更新的数学大全。

cues.en: Written in five years, may it last for five hundred.
cues.zh: 五年写成，愿它流传五百年。

cues.en: Cardano writes a chapter with a unique geometric proof for each of the 13 arrangements of the cubic equation.
cues.zh: 卡尔达诺写了一个章节，为三次方程的13种形式各给出一个独特的几何证明。

cues.en: Although he acknowledges the contributions of Tartaglia, Delferro, and Fior, Tartaglia is displeased to say the least. He writes insulting letters to Cardano and cc's a good fraction of the mathematics community.
cues.zh: 尽管他承认了塔尔塔利亚、德尔费罗和菲奥尔的贡献，塔尔塔利亚还是很不高兴，至少可以这么说。他写信辱骂卡尔达诺，还抄送给了相当一部分数学界人士。

cues.en: And he has a point. To this day, the general solution to the cubic is often called Cardano's method.
cues.zh: 他说得也有道理。直到今天，三次方程的通用解法通常还被称为卡尔达诺方法。

cues.en: But Ars Magna is a phenomenal achievement.
cues.zh: 但《大衍术》是一项非凡的成就。

cues.en: It pushes geometrical
cues.zh: 它把几何

cues.en: reasoning to its very breaking point,
cues.zh: 推理推到了极限，

cues.en: literally.
cues.zh: 字面意义上的极限。

cues.en: While Cardano is writing Ars Magna, he comes across some cubic equations that can't easily be solved in the usual way. Like x cubed equals 15 x plus four.
cues.zh: 卡尔达诺在写《大衍术》时，遇到了一些无法用常规方法轻松求解的三次方程。比如x的立方等于15x加4。

cues.en: Plugging this into the algorithm yields a solution that contains the square roots of negative numbers.
cues.zh: 把它代入算法，得到的解里含有负数的平方根。

cues.en: Cardano asks Tartaglia about the case, but he evades and implies Cardano is just not clever enough to use his formula properly.
cues.zh: Cardano 向 Tartaglia 请教这个情况，但 Tartaglia 支支吾吾，暗示 Cardano 只是不够聪明，没能正确使用他的公式。

cues.en: The reality is, Tartaglia has no idea what to do either.
cues.zh: 事实是，Tartaglia 自己也不知道该怎么办。

cues.en: Cardano walks back through the geometric derivation a similar problem to see exactly what goes wrong.
cues.zh: Cardano 用类似问题回溯几何推导过程，想看清楚究竟哪里出了错。

cues.en: While the three d cube slicing and rearrangement works just fine, the final quadratic completing the square step leads to a geometric paradox.
cues.zh: 三维立方体切片和重排都没问题，但最后配方法那一步却引出了几何悖论。

cues.en: Cardano finds part of a square that must have an area of 30,
cues.zh: Cardano 找到了一个正方形的一部分，它的面积必须是 30，

cues.en: but also sides of length five.
cues.zh: 但边长又是 5。

cues.en: Since the full square has an area of 25,
cues.zh: 而整个正方形的面积是 25，

cues.en: to complete the square, Cardano has to somehow add negative area.
cues.zh: 要配成这个正方形，Cardano 就得设法加上负面积。

cues.en: That is where the square roots of negatives come from, the idea of negative area.
cues.zh: 负数的平方根正是由此而来，来自负面积这个概念。

cues.en: Now this isn't the first time square roots of negatives show up in mathematics.
cues.zh: 这倒不是数学中第一次出现负数的平方根。

cues.en: In fact, earlier in Ars Magna is this problem.
cues.zh: 其实《大衍术》前面就有这个问题。

cues.en: Find two numbers that add to 10 and multiply to 40.
cues.zh: 找两个数，相加得 10，相乘得 40。

cues.en: You can combine these equations into the quadratic x squared plus 40 equals 10 x.
cues.zh: 把这两个方程合并，得到二次方程 x 平方加 40 等于 10x。

cues.en: But if you plug this into the quadratic formula,
cues.zh: 但把它代入求根公式，

cues.en: the solutions contain the square roots of negatives.
cues.zh: 解里就含有负数的平方根。

cues.en: The obvious conclusion is that a solution doesn't exist,
cues.zh: 显而易见的结论是解不存在，

cues.en: which you can verify by looking at the original problem. There are no two real numbers which add to 10 and multiply to 40.
cues.zh: 你回头看原问题就能验证。不存在两个实数，相加得 10 且相乘得 40。

cues.en: So mathematicians
cues.zh: 所以数学家们

cues.en: understood
cues.zh: 明白

cues.en: square roots of negative numbers were math's way of telling you there is no solution.
cues.zh: 负数的平方根是数学在告诉你，没有解。

cues.en: But this cubic equation is different.
cues.zh: 但这个三次方程不同。

cues.en: With a little guessing and checking, you can find that x equals four is a solution.
cues.zh: 稍加猜测和验证，你就能发现 x 等于 4 是一个解。

cues.en: So why doesn't the approach that works for all other cupics find the perfectly reasonable solution to this one?
cues.zh: 那么，为什么对所有其他三次方程都有效的方法，却找不到这个方程完全合理的解呢？

cues.en: Unable to see a way forward, Cardano avoids this case in Ars Magna saying the idea of the square root of negatives is as subtle as it is useless.
cues.zh: 由于看不到前进的方向，Cardano 在《大术》中回避了这种情况，称负数平方根的概念既微妙又无用。

cues.en: But around ten years later, the Italian engineer, Raphael Bombelli, picks up where Cardano left off. Undeterred by the square roots of negatives and the impossible geometry they imply,
cues.zh: 但大约十年后，意大利工程师 Raphael Bombelli 从 Cardano 停下的地方继续。他不被负数平方根及其所暗示的不可能几何所吓倒，

cues.en: he wants to find a way through the mess to the solution.
cues.zh: 他想找到一条穿过混乱到达解的道路。

cues.en: Observing that the square root of a negative cannot be called either positive or negative,
cues.zh: 观察到负数的平方根既不能被称为正数也不能被称为负数，

cues.en: he lets it be its own new type of number.
cues.zh: 他让它成为自己的一种新类型的数。

cues.en: Bombelli assumes the two terms in Cardano's solution can be represented as some combination of an ordinary number and this new type of number which involves the square root of negative one.
cues.zh: Bombelli 假设 Cardano 解中的两项可以表示为普通数和这种涉及负一平方根的新类型数的某种组合。

cues.en: And this way, Bombelli figures out that the two cube roots in Cardano's equation are equivalent to two plus or minus the square root of negative one. So when he takes the final step and adds them together, these square roots cancel out, leaving the correct answer four.
cues.zh: 这样一来，Bombelli 发现 Cardano 方程中的两个立方根等价于 2 加减负一的平方根。所以当他迈出最后一步将它们相加时，这些平方根相互抵消，留下了正确答案 4。

cues.en: This feels nothing short of miraculous.
cues.zh: 这简直堪称奇迹。

cues.en: Cardano's method does work, but you have to abandon the geometric proof that generated it in the first place.
cues.zh: Cardano 的方法确实有效，但你必须放弃最初催生它的几何证明。

cues.en: Negative areas,
cues.zh: 负面积，

cues.en: which make no sense in reality,
cues.zh: 在现实中毫无意义，

cues.en: must exist as an intermediate step on the way to the solution.
cues.zh: 却必须作为求解途中的中间步骤而存在。

cues.en: Over the next hundred years, modern mathematics takes shape. In the sixteen hundreds, Francois Viette introduces the modern symbolic notation for algebra, ending the millennia long tradition of math problems as drawings and wordy descriptions.
cues.zh: 接下来的一百年里，现代数学逐渐成形。17世纪，Francois Viette 引入了现代代数符号表示法，终结了数千年来以图形和冗长文字描述数学问题的传统。

cues.en: Geometry is no longer the source of truth.
cues.zh: 几何不再是真理之源。

cues.en: Rene Descartes makes heavy use of the square roots of negatives,
cues.zh: Rene Descartes 大量使用负数的平方根，

cues.en: popularizing them as a result.
cues.zh: 并因此让它们流行起来。

cues.en: And while he recognizes their utility, he calls them imaginary
cues.zh: 尽管他认识到它们的用处，却称它们为虚数

cues.en: numbers, a name that sticks, which is why Euler later introduces the letter I to represent the square root of negative one.
cues.zh: ——这个名字沿用至今，所以后来 Euler 引入字母 i 来表示负一的平方根。

cues.en: When combined with regular numbers, they form complex numbers.
cues.zh: 当与普通数结合时，它们构成复数。

cues.en: The cubic led to the invention of these new numbers and liberated algebra from geometry.
cues.zh: 三次方程催生了这些新数，并把代数从几何中解放出来。

cues.en: By letting go of what seems like the best description of reality, the geometry you can see and touch, you get a much more powerful and complete mathematics that can solve real problems.
cues.zh: 通过放下看似对现实的最佳描述——你能看见、能触摸的几何——你得到了一门更强大、更完整的数学，能够解决真实问题。

cues.en: And it turns out, the cubic is just the beginning.
cues.zh: 而事实证明，三次方程只是个开始。

cues.en: Erwin Schrodinger is searching for a wave equation that governs the behavior of quantum particles, building on de Broglie's insight that matter consists of waves.
cues.zh: Erwin Schrodinger 在 de Broglie 关于物质由波构成的洞见基础上，寻找一个支配量子粒子行为的波动方程。

cues.en: He comes up with one of the most important and famous equations in all of physics, the Schrodinger equation.
cues.zh: 他提出了全物理学中最重要、最著名的方程之一——薛定谔方程。

cues.en: And featured prominently within it is I, the square root of negative one.
cues.zh: 其中特别突出的，是 I，也就是负一的平方根。

cues.en: While mathematicians have grown accustomed to imaginary numbers,
cues.zh: 虽然数学家已经习惯了虚数，

cues.en: physicists have not and are uncomfortable seeing it show up in such a fundamental theory.
cues.zh: 物理学家却没有，而且看到它出现在如此基础的理论中会感到不安。

cues.en: Schrodinger himself writes,
cues.zh: 薛定谔本人写道，

cues.en: what is unpleasant here and indeed directly to be objected to is the use of complex numbers.
cues.zh: 这里令人不快、甚至直接该反对的，是使用了复数。

cues.en: The wave function psi is surely fundamentally a real function.
cues.zh: 波函数 psi 本质上当然是一个实函数。

cues.en: This seems like a fair objection. So why does an imaginary number that first appeared in the solution to the cubic turn up in fundamental physics?
cues.zh: 这看起来是个合理的反对。那么，一个最初出现在三次方程解中的虚数，为什么会出现在基础物理中？

cues.en: Well, it's because of some unique properties of imaginary numbers.
cues.zh: 嗯，这是因为虚数有一些独特的性质。

cues.en: Imaginary numbers exist on a dimension perpendicular
cues.zh: 虚数存在于一个维度上，它垂直于

cues.en: to the real number line.
cues.zh: 实数轴。

cues.en: Together, they form the complex plane.
cues.zh: 它们一起构成复平面。

cues.en: Watch what happens when we repeatedly multiply by I.
cues.zh: 看看当我们反复乘以 I 时会发生什么。

cues.en: Starting with one,
cues.zh: 从 1 开始，

cues.en: one times I is I.
cues.zh: 1 乘以 I 是 I。

cues.en: I times I is negative one by definition.
cues.zh: I 乘以 I 按定义是 -1。

cues.en: Negative one times I is negative I and negative I times I is one. We've come back to where we started and if we keep multiplying by I, the point will keep rotating around.
cues.zh: -1 乘以 I 是 -I，而 -I 乘以 I 是 1。我们回到了起点，如果继续乘以 I，这个点就会不断旋转。

cues.en: So when you're multiplying by I, what you're really doing is rotating
cues.zh: 所以当你乘以 I 时，你实际上是在

cues.en: by 90 degrees in a complex plane.
cues.zh: 复平面中旋转 90 度。

cues.en: Now there is a function that repeatedly
cues.zh: 现在有一个函数，它会反复

cues.en: multiplies by I as you go down the x axis and that is e to the I x.
cues.zh: 乘以 I，随着你沿 x 轴前进，那就是 e 的 Ix 次方。

cues.en: It creates a spiral by essentially spreading out these rotations
cues.zh: 它本质上是通过展开这些旋转来形成一条螺旋

cues.en: all along the x axis.
cues.zh: 沿着 x 轴。

cues.en: If you look at the real part of the spiral, it's a cosine wave. And if you look at the imaginary part, it's a sine wave.
cues.zh: 看螺旋的实部，它是余弦波。看虚部，它是正弦波。

cues.en: The two quintessential functions that describe waves are both contained in e to the I x.
cues.zh: 描述波的两种典型函数，都包含在 e 的 ix 次方里。

cues.en: So when Schrodinger goes to write down a wave equation, he naturally assumes that the solutions to his equation will look something like e to the I x, specifically e to the I k x minus omega t.
cues.zh: 所以薛定谔写下波动方程时，自然假设方程的解会类似 e 的 ix 次方，具体是 e 的 i(kx−ωt) 次方。

cues.en: You might wonder why he would use that formulation and not just a simple sine wave, but the exponential has some useful properties. If you take the derivative with respect to position or time,
cues.zh: 你可能纳闷他为什么用这种形式，而不直接用简单的正弦波，但指数函数有一些有用的性质。如果对位置或时间求导，

cues.en: that derivative is proportional to the original function itself.
cues.zh: 这个导数就与原函数本身成正比。

cues.en: And that's not true if you use the sine function whose derivative is cosine.
cues.zh: 但如果你用正弦函数就不成立，因为它的导数是余弦。

cues.en: Plus, since the Schrodinger equation is linear,
cues.zh: 另外，由于薛定谔方程是线性的，

cues.en: you can add together an arbitrary number of solutions of this form creating any sort of wave shape you like and it too will be a solution to Schrodinger's equation.
cues.zh: 你可以把任意多个这种形式的解相加，构造出任何你想要的波形，它也会是薛定谔方程的解。

cues.en: The physicist Freeman Dyson later writes, Schrodinger put the square root of minus one into the equation and suddenly it made sense. Suddenly,
cues.zh: 物理学家 Freeman Dyson 后来写道，薛定谔把负一的平方根放进方程，突然就说得通了。突然，

cues.en: it became a wave equation instead of a heat conduction equation.
cues.zh: 它变成了波动方程，而不是热传导方程。

cues.en: And Schrodinger found to his delight that the equation has solutions corresponding to the quantized orbits in the Bohr model of the atom.
cues.zh: 薛定谔欣喜地发现，这个方程的解对应于玻尔原子模型中的量子化轨道。

cues.en: It turns out that the Schrodinger equation describes correctly
cues.zh: 事实证明，薛定谔方程正确地描述了

cues.en: everything we know about the behavior of atoms.
cues.zh: 我们所知的原子行为的一切。

cues.en: It is the basis of all of chemistry and most of physics.
cues.zh: 它是所有化学和大部分物理学的基础。

cues.en: And that square root of minus one means that nature works with complex numbers and not with real numbers.
cues.zh: 而负一的平方根意味着自然运作于复数而非实数之上。

cues.en: This discovery came as a complete surprise
cues.zh: 这个发现完全出乎意料，

cues.en: to Schrodinger as well as to everybody else.
cues.zh: 对薛定谔本人和其他所有人都一样。

cues.en: So imaginary numbers
cues.zh: 所以虚数，

cues.en: discovered as a quirky intermediate step on the way to solving the cubic turn out to be fundamental to our description of reality.
cues.zh: 最初只是作为解三次方程的奇怪中间步骤被发现，最终却成为我们描述现实的基础。

cues.en: Only by giving up math's connection to reality could it guide us to a deeper truth about the way the universe works.
cues.zh: 只有放弃数学与现实的联系，它才能引导我们走向关于宇宙运作方式的更深层真理。
